facts.statement: Hulsanpes remains were discovered in 1970 and formally described in 1982 by Halszka Osmólska.
facts.quote: The remains were found in 1970 and formally described in 1982 by Halszka Osmólska, who noted that the genus is represented by an immature individual.

facts.statement: Hulsanpes lived in the Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia approximately 75 to 72 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Hulsanpes (meaning "Khulsan foot") is a genus of halszkaraptorine theropod dinosaurs that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Barun Goyot Formation of Mongolia, about 75-72 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first fossils of Hulsanpes were found in 1970 at Khulsan in the Gobi Desert during a Polish-Mongolian expedition.
facts.quote: The first fossil remains of Hulsanpes were discovered in 1970 during the third Polish-Mongolian expedition at Khulsan in the Gobi Desert.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial braincase fragment and a right metatarsus with three pedal phalanges from an immature individual.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial braincase fragment and the right metatarsus composed by the second, third and fourth metatarsals and three pedal phalanges from an apparently immature individual.

facts.statement: The roughly textured bones of the holotype indicate it was likely a post-hatchling chick.
facts.quote: The roughly textured bones are indicators of an early stage of life, probably a post-hatchling chick.

facts.statement: The preserved portion of the braincase measures just 1 cm in length.
facts.quote: The partial braincase is a small element, measuring just 1 cm in length, it is embedded in a small portion of the sandstone layer.

facts.statement: In 2017, Hulsanpes was placed in the new clade Halszkaraptorinae alongside Halszkaraptor and Mahakala.
facts.quote: in 2017 during the description of Halszkaraptor a new clade, the Halszkaraptorinae, was coined by Cau and colleagues, containing the new genus Halszkaraptor and its close relatives which were identified as being the long enigmatic Hulsanpes and Mahakala.

facts.statement: The Halszkaraptorinae is considered the most primitive known dromaeosaurid group, closely related to unenlagiines.
facts.quote: The analysis showed that the Halszkaraptorinae was the most primitive known dromaeosaurid group, slightly related to unenlagiines.

facts.statement: Hulsanpes likely spent much of its time in aquatic environments like rivers, swimming using both forelimbs and hindlimbs.
facts.quote: Hulsanpes had a similar life-style to those of the modern-day sawbills or waterfowls, spending most of their time in aquatic environments (such as rivers) using fore and hindlimb-assisted swimming.

facts.statement: Adaptations in the holotype metatarsus suggest Hulsanpes may have had a more terrestrial, subcursorial lifestyle.
facts.quote: However, it appears to be that Hulsanpes may have been more terrestrial based on the holotype metatarsus, which features adaptations for a more subcursorial life-style, supporting the diversification within this subfamily.

facts.statement: The environment of Hulsanpes included large rivers, other water bodies, and prominent dune-like terrains.
facts.quote: Most of the environments present consisted of large rivers with other water bodies, and prominent dune-like terrains.

facts.statement: Hulsanpes shared its habitat with dinosaurs including Bagaceratops, Gobipteryx, Parvicursor, Saichania, Tarchia, and Tylocephale.
facts.quote: Here, Hulsanpes shared their habitat with diverse dinosaurs such as Bagaceratops, Gobipteryx, Parvicursor, Saichania, Tarchia and Tylocephale.

facts.statement: Hulsanpes represents the first known record of the basal dromaeosaurid subfamily Halszkaraptorinae.
facts.quote: Hulsanpes represents the first record of the basal dromaeosaurid subfamily Halszkaraptorinae.

facts.statement: It was debated whether Hulsanpes belonged to Averaptora incertae sedis due to interpretations of its metatarsals, but later analysis proved those interpretations incorrect.
facts.quote: Agnolin and Novas in 2013 assigned it to Averaptora incertae sedis based on the fact that the extremely gracile metatarsals are similar to Avialae and metatarsal III interpreted to be pinched at the upper region. This latter statement has been proven to be incorrect though.
